description_en: The Halĩpatāḥ Phalcā lies to the west of the main road of the Sunaguthi. Queen Siddhimaṅgalādevī Thakunī, the wife of King Śrīnivāsa Malla, commissioned this Phalcā in 1686 CE. The main Bālakumarī Guṭhī looks after it because it is one of the important ritual sites in the town. The Phalcā was reconstructed in 1949 and in 2014.The Phalcā has three front and two side bays and is furnished with a wooden balustrade. Its depth is somewhat greater than is usual forphalcās. Five layers of terracotta bricks separate the ground floor from the first floor. The gable roof has no struts and is roofed withjhĩgaṭītiles. Three metal pinnacles have been placed on top of the roof.Halĩpatāḥ Phalcā is a platform closely related to the symbol of the snake (and in fact, there seems to be a carved stone snake on the plinth around the site). The Halĩpatāḥ is a ritual cloth (symbolising snakes) which is attached to the pole when it is raised in front of the arcaded platform once a year. Before this occurs, the Halĩpatāḥ is kept inside the Phalcā for three nights and is accompanied byguṭhīyāras. When not in use, the Halĩpatāḥ and the statues of the deities are kept in the house of aguṭhīyāra(the duties of looking after the ritual objects and caretaking rotate annually from house to house). A legend says that the Halĩpatāḥ once flew to Bhaktapur, where they are now kept. Tradition dictates that when meat is bought to the south of the Halĩpatāḥ Phalcā, people going north should walk around the back of the Phalcā so that they keep as far a distance from the temple as possible – the same goes for funeral processions.Please note: All visuals of this monument folder and more are sustainably stored in heidICON, the object and multimedia database of Heidelberg University:https://heidicon.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/pool/nhdp/systematik/LAL4012
description_ne: सुनागुथिको मूल सडकको पश्चिमपट्टि यो फल्चा अवस्थित छ । फल्चामा अगाडि तीन कवल र दायाँबायाँ दुई कवल छन् । फल्चाको कवलको आकार सामान्यभन्दा केही बढि देखिन्छ । फल्चाको माथिल्लो होचो तलालाई अलग देखाउन निदालमाथि टेराकोटा ईंटको प्रयोग गरी पाँच तहको बुट्टा बनाइएको छ । टायलले छाइएको छानामाथि तीनवटा धातुका गजुर राखिएका छन् ।श्रीनिवास मल्लकी रानी सिद्धिमङ्गलादेवी थकुनीले यो फल्चा सन् १६८६ मा बनाएकी थिइन् । यो फल्चाको सन् २०१४ मा पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो । बालकुमारी गुठीले यस फल्चाको रेखदेख गर्ने गर्दछ ।नागको आकृतिसँग यो फल्चाको संबन्ध रहेको छ । चैत्र शुक्ल पूर्णिमाका दिन सुनागुथिमा प्यखःजात्रा हुने गर्दछ । जात्राको दुई दिन अघि अर्थात् त्रयोदशीका दिन नागको प्रतीकस्वरूप हलिंपताः भनिने एउटा कपडा झुण्ड्याइएको यःसिँ यस फल्चाको ठीक अगाडि ठड्याउने परम्परा छ । फल्चा अठाडि यःसिँ खडा हुँदै गर्दा जात्रा व्यवस्थापन गर्ने गुठीका गुठीयारहरू फल्चामा बसी अवलोकन गर्ने चलन छ । यःसिँ खडा गरिएपछिको दुई रात गुठीयारहरू यसै फल्चामा रात काट्ने गर्छन् । खडा गरिएको यःसिँमा हुने पताःको सुरक्षार्थ फल्चामा रात बस्ने परम्परा बसालेको हो भन्ने विश्वास सुथागुथिवासीमा पाइन्छ । सुनागुथिवासीहरू यो हलिंपताःको विषयमा एउटा रोचक कथा भन्ने गर्दछन् जस अनुसार पहिला कुनै समयमा हलिंपताः उँडेर भक्तपुर पुगेको थियो जुन अहिले पनि त्यहाँ सुरक्षित रहेको छ । कसैले मासु बोकेर हिंडेको छ भने फल्चाको अगाडिबाट नहिंडेर पछाडिपट्टिबाट हिंड्ने अनि लास बोकेर हिंड्दा पनि त्यसै गर्ने चलन रहेको छ ।

historical_events.event_description: Queen Siddhimaṅgalādevī Thakunī (wife of King Śrīnivāsa Malla) initiated the construction of this Phalcā in 1686 CE. She endowed the site with four different areas of land so that aguṭhīmight be organised to look after the construction and take care of the monument. The inscription placed in the Phalcā mentions that the Queen commissioned the monument in memory of the King, and an image of Umāmaheśvara was installed in the Phalcā in his name.
Locals reconstructed the Phalcā by collecting donations.
The Phalcā was badly damaged in the 2015 earthquakes (see photographs in 'Monuments after 2015').
